name: partials
description: Changes the strength of the simple waves that make a synth's tone. The first number controls the main tone; later numbers control higher tones called harmonics.
notes: Use a synth such as sawtooth and a list such as [1, 0.5, 0.2]. Values from 0 to 1 set each wave's strength.

name: phases
description: Moves the starting point of each simple wave inside a synth sound. This changes how the waves line up.
notes: Use with synth sounds and partials. Give a list such as [0, 0.5, 0]; 0.5 means half a wave turn.

name: noise
description: Mixes a hiss into a synth sound. A larger value adds more noise.
notes: Use with a synth such as sine or sawtooth. Start with a small amount such as 0.1.

name: density
description: Changes how tightly packed the clicks are in crackling noise.
notes: Use with sound: crackle. This does not add more notes to an ordinary melody.

name: vib
description: Makes a note wobble up and down in pitch. The number sets how many wobbles happen each second.
notes: Use vibmod to set how far the pitch moves; for example, vib: 5 with vibmod: 0.2.

name: vibmod
description: Sets how far vibrato moves above and below the note, measured in semitones. One semitone is one step to the next piano key.
notes: Use with vib, which sets the wobble speed.

name: fm
description: Changes a synth's tone by using another wave to shake its pitch very quickly. A larger amount usually makes a more complex or brighter tone.
notes: Start with sound: sine and fm: 2. Use fmh to change the second wave's speed and the fmattack/fmdecay/fmsustain controls to change the effect during each note.

name: fmh
description: Sets the speed of the extra wave used by fm compared with the note's own wave. A value of 2 makes the extra wave twice as fast.
notes: Use with a nonzero fm amount. Whole numbers and fractions can give quite different tones.

name: fmattack
description: Sets how many seconds the fm effect takes to reach its strongest amount after a note starts.
notes: Use with fm. A longer value makes the tone change more slowly at the start.

name: fmdecay
description: Sets how many seconds the fm effect takes to fall from its strongest amount to its continuing level.
notes: Use with fm and fmsustain. Set fmsustain below 1 to hear the fall clearly.

name: fmsustain
description: Sets how much of the fm effect remains after its initial rise and fall. A value of 0 removes it at that stage; 1 keeps its full amount.
notes: Use with fm and fmdecay. This controls the tone change, not the note's volume.

name: fmenv
description: Chooses how the fm effect rises and falls: lin uses a straight ramp, while exp uses a curved ramp.
notes: Use with fm and its timing controls. Write lin or exp rather than an amount; the pinned sound library warns that exp may be unreliable.

name: lfo
description: Makes a sound setting move up and down repeatedly while a note plays. This repeating motion is called modulation.
notes: This advanced control needs a supported setting to move and a configuration. The app cannot yet express its full configuration; the number in lfo: 2 does not set its speed.

name: attack
description: Sets how many seconds a sound takes to rise from silence to its starting volume. Short times give a sharp start; long times give a gentle swell.
notes: Use a note long enough to hear the rise. Combine with decay, sustain, and release to shape the whole note.

name: decay
description: Sets how many seconds the volume takes to fall from its starting peak to the sustain level.
notes: Use sustain below 1 to hear this fall. Attack controls the rise before it.

name: sustain
description: Sets the volume level kept after attack and decay, as a share of the peak. For example, 0.5 keeps half of that level.
notes: This is a level, not a time. Use clip to change note length and release to change its ending fade.

name: release
description: Sets how many seconds a sound takes to fade after the note ends.
notes: A longer release lets nearby notes overlap. Include the fading sound when exporting if you want to keep the ending.

name: adsr
description: Sets a note's rise, fall, held level, and ending fade in one line, in that order.
notes: Write four comma-separated numbers: attack seconds, decay seconds, sustain level, release seconds. For example, 0.01, 0.2, 0.5, 0.3.

name: lowpass
description: Softens a sound by turning down the high parts above a chosen frequency. Lower numbers usually make the sound darker.
notes: The cutoff is in Hz, meaning vibrations per second. Try lowpass: 1200 Hz; use lpq to emphasize the sound near that cutoff.

name: lpq
description: Emphasizes the sound near the lowpass cutoff, which can give it a ringing or whistling edge.
notes: Set lowpass too; lpq does not choose the cutoff. Start low and listen as you increase it.

name: highpass
description: Thins a sound by turning down the low parts below a chosen frequency.
notes: The cutoff is in Hz. For example, highpass: 300 Hz reduces bass; hpq emphasizes the sound near that cutoff.

name: hpq
description: Emphasizes the sound near the highpass cutoff, which can give it a ringing edge.
notes: Use with highpass. High values can make the selected area much louder.

name: bandpass
description: Keeps a band of frequencies around the chosen center and turns down sound above and below it.
notes: Give the center in Hz. Use bpq to make the kept band narrower or wider.

name: bpq
description: Controls how narrow the bandpass filter's kept band is. Higher values focus on a narrower part of the sound.
notes: Use with bandpass to choose the center frequency.

name: ftype
description: Chooses the filter design, which changes how it cuts and colors the sound.
notes: Use with a filter such as lowpass. Choose 0 for 12db, 1 for ladder, or 2 for 24db; ladder has a more aggressive sound.

name: vowel
description: Shapes a sound so it resembles a mouth saying a vowel.
notes: Use a, e, i, o, or u. A rich sound such as sawtooth makes the change easier to hear.

name: lpattack
description: Sets how many seconds the lowpass filter movement takes to rise to its peak after a note starts.
notes: Use lowpass for the starting cutoff and lpenv for how far it moves. These controls shape brightness, not volume.

name: lpdecay
description: Sets how many seconds the lowpass filter movement takes to fall from its peak to its continuing level.
notes: Use with lowpass, lpenv, and lpsustain. A short fall can make a bright note quickly turn darker.

name: lpsustain
description: Sets the lowpass filter movement's continuing level after its rise and fall. A value of 0 removes that movement; 1 keeps its full amount.
notes: Use with lowpass and lpenv. This is a level, not a number of seconds.

name: lprelease
description: Sets how many seconds the lowpass filter movement takes to return after the note ends.
notes: Use with lowpass and lpenv. Give release enough time for the sound to remain audible during this change.
example:
lowpass: 500 Hz
lpenv: 2
release: 0.5 seconds
lprelease: 0.4

name: lpenv
description: Sets how far the lowpass cutoff moves during each note. This can make a note start bright and then become darker.
notes: Use with lowpass. Shape the movement with lpattack, lpdecay, lpsustain, and lprelease.

name: pattack
description: Sets how many seconds the pitch takes to rise through its planned movement at the start of a note.
notes: Use penv to set how far the pitch moves. This changes pitch rather than volume.

name: pdecay
description: Sets how many seconds the pitch movement takes to fall from its peak to its continuing level.
notes: Use with penv. A short fall can help make a synth sound like a drum.

name: prelease
description: Sets how many seconds the pitch movement takes to return after the note ends.
notes: Use with penv and a long enough release to hear the ending movement.

name: penv
description: Sets how far pitch moves during a note, in semitones. One semitone is one step to the next piano key; 12 is an octave.
notes: Use pattack, pdecay, and prelease to set the timing. Negative values turn the movement upside down.

name: pcurve
description: Chooses whether the pitch movement follows a straight ramp or a curved ramp.
notes: Use with penv. Write 0 for a straight ramp or 1 for a curved ramp, often useful for drum sounds.

name: panchor
description: Places the pitch movement's range above or below the written note. At 0 it starts from the note and reaches upward; at 1 the range ends at the note.
notes: Use with penv. With positive penv, 0.5 centers the range around the written note; the timing still comes from pattack and pdecay.

name: velocity
description: Sets how strongly a note is played. In this app's sound engine, it changes loudness.
notes: Use values such as 0.3 for softer notes and 1 for full strength. Volume still changes the overall level too.

name: compressor
description: Turns down sound that rises above a chosen loudness level. This can reduce the difference between quiet and loud parts.
notes: The first value is the threshold in decibels; try -20. This effect does not automatically fix a mix that is too loud.

name: postgain
description: Changes the volume after the sound's effects have been applied. A value of 1 keeps the level; 0.5 halves it.
notes: Useful for turning down a sound after distort or other effects make it louder.

name: xfade
description: Blends the current pattern with a second pattern. At 0 you hear the first, at 0.5 both, and at 1 the second.
notes: Give the blend amount and an existing named pattern, such as xfade: 0.5, $other. Changing the amount over time creates the fade.
example:
pattern: other
  sound: triangle
  notes: G4 B4
track: melody
  sound: sine
  notes: C4 E4
  xfade: 0.5, $other

name: pan
description: Places a sound between the left and right speakers. 0% is left, 50% is the middle, and 100% is right.
notes: Use stereo speakers or headphones to hear the position clearly.

name: jux
description: Plays the original pattern on the left and a changed copy on the right.
notes: Indent the change beneath it, such as rev: or faster: 2. Stereo speakers or headphones make the difference easier to hear.

name: jux by
description: Plays the original and a changed copy with a chosen stereo spread. A value of 0 keeps them centered; 1 puts them fully left and right.
notes: Give the spread, then indent the change beneath it. Use 0.5 for a smaller separation.

name: coarse
description: Makes the audio update in bigger steps, giving it a rougher digital sound.
notes: A value of 1 keeps the original update rate; larger values reduce it. Combine with crush for a stronger old digital sound.

name: crush
description: Reduces how precisely each tiny piece of audio is stored, making the sound grainy or crunchy. The number sets the bit depth.
notes: Smaller values make the effect stronger. Try 8 before very low values such as 2.

name: distort
description: Bends the sound wave to make it rougher, buzzier, or more intense.
notes: Start with a small amount. Use volume or postgain to keep the louder result comfortable.

name: orbit
description: Puts a sound into a numbered group that shares effects such as echo and reverb.
notes: Give tracks different orbit numbers when their shared effects should stay separate. Duckorbit uses this number to choose which group gets quieter.

name: delay
description: Adds echoes of the sound. The value controls how much echo you hear.
notes: Use delaytime for the gap between echoes and delayfeedback for how long they keep repeating. Start with an amount below 1.

name: delaytime
description: Sets the gap between echoes in seconds.
notes: Use a nonzero delay amount. For example, delaytime: 0.25 seconds puts a quarter-second gap between repeats.

name: delayfeedback
description: Sets how much of each echo is sent back to create another echo. Higher values make the repeats last longer.
notes: Use with delay. Keep it below 1 for fading repeats; values at or above 1 can keep building up.

name: reverb
description: Adds a fading wash of reflections, like hearing your sound in a room.
notes: The amount sets how much reflected sound you hear. Use roomsize and roomfade to change the space and its fade.

name: roomsize
description: Changes the size of the imagined room used for reverb.
notes: Use with a nonzero reverb amount. Values from 0 to 10 control size; larger rooms usually sound more spacious.

name: roomfade
description: Sets how many seconds the reverb takes to fade away.
notes: Use with reverb. Longer fades may need more extra seconds in your export to keep the full ending.

name: roomlp
description: Sets the highest frequencies kept at the start of the reverb, in Hz. Lower values make the reflections darker.
notes: Use with reverb. Roomdim controls the darker cutoff near the end of the fade; avoid changing these settings rapidly.

name: roomdim
description: Sets the reverb's high-frequency cutoff near the quiet end of its fade, in Hz.
notes: Use with reverb and roomlp. A lower roomdim than roomlp makes the reflections lose brightness as they fade.

name: iresponse
description: Uses a loaded recording as the shape of the reverb. The recording describes how a space or effect responds to a quick sound.
notes: Use with reverb and a recording that the audio engine has already loaded. A name alone does not download a recording.

name: phaser
description: Adds a repeating sweeping sound by mixing the original with a filtered copy. The number sets the sweep speed.
notes: Use phaserdepth for strength, phasercenter for the middle frequency, and phasersweep for the range.

name: phaserdepth
description: Sets how strongly the phaser changes the sound. A value of 0 removes the effect and 1 gives its full amount.
notes: Use with phaser to start the sweeping motion.

name: phasercenter
description: Sets the middle frequency of the phaser's sweep, in Hz.
notes: Use with phaser. Phasersweep controls how far it travels around this center.

name: phasersweep
description: Sets how wide a frequency range the phaser sweeps through, in Hz.
notes: Use with phaser and phasercenter. A larger range makes a broader sweep.

name: am
description: Makes the volume repeatedly rise and fall. The number sets how many pulses happen each second.
notes: This app uses tremolo for this command. Use tremolodepth to control how strongly the volume pulses.

name: tremolosync
description: Makes the volume pulse in time with the music. The number sets how many pulses happen in one pattern cycle.
notes: Use this to keep pulsing lined up when tempo changes. Use tremolodepth to set the strength.

name: tremolodepth
description: Sets how much the volume drops during each tremolo pulse.
notes: Use with am or tremolosync. Start between 0 and 1; 0 keeps the volume steady.

name: tremoloskew
description: Changes the balance between the rising and falling parts of each volume pulse.
notes: Use with am or tremolosync. Values from 0 to 1 move between different pulse shapes; 0.5 gives a balanced shape.

name: tremolophase
description: Moves the starting point of the volume pulse. A value of 0.5 shifts it by half a pulse.
notes: Use with am or tremolosync. This helps offset the pulses of two tracks.

name: tremoloshape
description: Chooses the shape followed by the repeating volume pulses.
notes: Use with am or tremolosync. Choose sine for smooth waves, tri for straight rises and falls, square for sudden switches, or saw/ramp for one-way ramps.

name: duckorbit
description: Briefly lowers the volume of another numbered sound group whenever this track plays a note.
notes: Set orbit on the track you want to lower, then use that same number in duckorbit on the triggering track. Duckdepth sets the amount and duckattack sets recovery time.

name: duckattack
description: Sets how many seconds a ducked sound group takes to return to its normal volume.
notes: Use on the triggering track together with duckorbit and duckdepth. A longer time makes the quiet dip last longer.

name: duckdepth
description: Sets how far the target sound group's volume drops when ducking happens.
notes: Use with duckorbit. A value of 0 causes no dip; 1 gives the full dip.

name: choose
description: Picks one of the supplied values using a changing number. A random number pattern makes the choice random.
notes: For random choices, use a rand signal before choose and give several choices separated by commas. Assign the chosen values to a setting such as notes or sound.

name: wchoose
description: Picks from choices that each have a weight. A larger weight makes that choice more likely.
notes: Give value-and-weight pairs, such as ["C4", 3], ["E4", 1]. Use the resulting values as notes or another sound setting.

name: choose cycles
description: Chooses one of the supplied patterns for each full cycle, with an equal chance for each choice.
notes: Supply patterns or named pattern references. A cycle is one full pattern repeat, usually one bar before timing changes.
example:
pattern: first
  sound: triangle
  notes: C4 E4
pattern: second
  sound: sine
  notes: G4 B4
track: melody
  choose cycles: $first, $second

name: wchoose cycles
description: Chooses one pattern for each full cycle, giving some choices a greater chance than others.
notes: Give pattern-and-weight pairs. A weight of 3 makes a choice three times as likely as a weight of 1.

name: degrade
description: Randomly leaves out about half of the notes or hits, leaving gaps in their places.
notes: Put it after a pattern. This changes which events play, rather than making the audio sound grainy.

name: degrade by
description: Sets the chance that each note or hit will be left out.
notes: Use a value from 0 to 1: 0 keeps everything, 0.25 drops about a quarter, and 1 drops everything.

name: undegrade
description: Keeps the random notes or hits that degrade would leave out.
notes: Apply it to the same original pattern and timing to hear the complementary part. It cannot restore events already removed earlier.

name: undegrade by
description: Keeps the random notes or hits that degrade by would remove at the same amount.
notes: Use 0 to keep none or 1 to keep everything. Start from the original pattern when comparing the two parts.

name: sometimes
description: Applies the indented change with a 50% chance, so some events change and others stay as they were.
notes: Indent a change beneath it. Use some cycles instead when you want one decision for a whole cycle.

name: sometimes by
description: Applies the indented change with the chance you choose.
notes: Give a value from 0 to 1, such as 0.25 for a 25% chance, then indent the change beneath it.

name: some cycles
description: Randomly applies the indented change to about half of the whole cycles.
notes: One decision covers each full pattern repeat. Indent the change beneath this command.

name: some cycles by
description: Randomly changes whole cycles using the chance you choose.
notes: Give 0 to change no cycles, 0.5 for about half, or 1 for every cycle, then indent the change beneath it.

name: often
description: Applies the indented change with a 75% chance.
notes: Indent the change beneath it. This is a chance for each event, not a promise that exactly three of every four events will change.

name: rarely
description: Applies the indented change with a 25% chance.
notes: Indent the change beneath it. The results can include several changed events or several unchanged events in a row.

name: almost never
description: Applies the indented change with a 10% chance.
notes: Indent the change beneath it. Over time, roughly one event in ten changes.

name: almost always
description: Applies the indented change with a 90% chance.
notes: Indent the change beneath it. Over time, roughly nine events in ten change.

name: never
description: Leaves the pattern unchanged instead of applying the indented change.
notes: Useful for temporarily turning off a change while keeping its lines in your song.

name: always
description: Applies the indented change every time.
notes: Indent the change beneath it. You can later replace always with sometimes to make the same change occasional.

name: first of
description: Applies the indented change during the first cycle in each repeating group of cycles.
notes: For example, first of: 4 changes the first cycle of every group of four. Indent the change beneath it.

name: last of
description: Applies the indented change during the last cycle in each repeating group of cycles.
notes: For example, last of: 4 changes the fourth cycle of every group of four. This is useful for a drum fill.

name: when
description: Applies the indented change when your condition is true.
notes: Give an on/off pattern such as <1 0>, then indent a change beneath it. Here 1 applies the change and 0 leaves the pattern alone.
You can also write a condition such as cycle % 2 == 0. Cycle counts bars starting at 0; this condition chooses every other bar.

name: chunk
description: Splits a cycle into equal parts, then changes one part per repeat, moving forward through the parts.
notes: Give the number of parts and indent the change. Chunk: 4 repeats each source cycle four times while visiting its four parts.

name: chunk back
description: Works like chunk, but visits the parts from last to first.
notes: Give the number of parts and indent the change beneath it.

name: fast chunk
description: Changes one part per cycle, moving through the parts while the original pattern keeps advancing.
notes: Use this instead of chunk when a pattern changes from cycle to cycle and you want those changes to keep moving. Give the part count and indent the change.

name: struct
description: Gives a pattern a new rhythm using a pattern of on and off steps. On steps create the places where notes or hits can start.
notes: Use a pattern such as 1 0 1 0, where 1 is on and 0 is off. Mask instead keeps the original event starts.

name: mask
description: Keeps or removes existing notes and hits according to an on/off pattern.
notes: Use 1 for on and 0 for off, such as mask: 1 0 1 0. This keeps the original timing of the events that pass through.
